mission.title: Research Design, Evidence and Epistemic Caution

theory.title: Research Design, Evidence and Epistemic Caution
theory.explanation: This mission develops advanced research design. Effective C2 communication requires writers and speakers to make purpose, audience, evidence and degree of certainty explicit. Analyse the context before choosing a register; distinguish established information from interpretation; organise complex material so that decisions and qualifications remain visible.
theory.tip: Use precise terminology, attribute claims, qualify uncertainty and make the requested action explicit.

patterns.label: Define purpose and audience
patterns.pattern: Identify what the audience needs to know or decide.
examples: State the decision required before presenting supporting detail.

patterns.label: Support and qualify
patterns.pattern: Connect each claim to evidence and state relevant limitations.
examples: The findings suggest a pattern, although the sample is not representative.

patterns.label: Structure for action
patterns.pattern: Use signposting, headings and explicit ownership.
examples: The recommendation is assigned to a named lead for review by an agreed date.

patterns.label: Review for integrity
patterns.pattern: Check terminology, attribution, tone and consistency.
examples: Distinguish verified outcomes from projected benefits.

content.passage:
A university team examined whether a new mentoring programme improved first-year retention. The initial report compared participants with the whole student population and described the difference as evidence of impact. A methodological review identified a problem: students had volunteered for mentoring, and those who volunteered were already more likely to seek academic support.

The revised analysis matched participants with non-participants who had similar entry profiles, while acknowledging that unmeasured differences could remain. The results still showed an association, but the team removed the phrase 'the programme caused the improvement'. It instead stated that the findings were consistent with a beneficial effect, pending a design capable of stronger causal inference.

The report included the sample size, missing-data rate and a plan for replication at another institution. These details did not weaken the work; they clarified what could reasonably be concluded. The team argued that methodological caution is not reluctance to make claims, but discipline in matching the scope of a claim to the design that supports it.
